newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares end flat, market seen nervous.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares end flat, market seen nervous.

text.p: Slovenia's SBI index petered out to close almost unchanged on Wednesday after a string of solid daily gains prompted some profit-taking. Traders forecast increasing selling pressure.
"There was some profit-taking today and it was easy to feel nervousness on the market, as many shares have already reached very high levels," said Polona Cec, a trader at Factor Bank.
The SBI index firmed 0.02 percent or 0.36 points to 1,611.42. In seven trading days the blue-chip index has risen almost five percent.

"Domestic demand is greater and it looks like domestic buyers do not rely on foreigners as much as they used to before. It is difficult to say what will happen next week as selling pressure is on the increase," Cec said.
Overall 11 shares rose, seven fell and three were flat while seven were untraded. Turnover rose to 280.3 million from 261.9 million.
Trading firm Kovinotehna was the most actively traded stock, rising 1.40 percent to 580 tolars on volume of 5,676 shares.
Market participants said Kovinotehna's business results and its outlook with new branches opening in Russia were the reason for the strong demand in the stock over the last few days.
But the poor liquidity of the share made its position vulnerable, they added.
Petrol trader Istrabenz was the top gainer, jumping 3.30 percent to 3,410 tolars on volume of 2,525 shares.
Bank Probanka was the leading decliner, falling 2.62 percent to 22,300 tolars on volume of 12 shares.
